title: Drop the phone-tool Step; keep the every-ancestor rule in the Android dump check
context: Wave 2 pre-launch audit: Step phone-tool-overlay-reach would clip a node's reachable rect only by the window and scrolling ancestors. Flutter's Android AccessibilityBridge.hitTest (explore-by-touch) rejects points outside each node's own rect and walks childrenInHitTestOrder, so ordinary content really is clipped by every ancestor; only overlay content grafted under its anchor in traversal order is misjudged. The Step would hide real tap-area bugs (the to-do case) and breaks 2 guarding tests in test/tooling/android_dump_rules_reachable_test.dart. Steps card-pill-reach (card bounds grow over the pill) and more-formats-reach (menu hosted in a plain OverlayEntry) fix both overlays and clear the tool's false alarms.
options: Drop the Step and keep the tool rule
Narrow the tool change to a named exception list for the known overlays
Keep the Step as written and rewrite the 2 guarding tests
outcome: Owner chose: drop it. phone-tool-overlay-reach is removed from wave 2. Criterion 10.23 becomes: after card-pill-reach and more-formats-reach, the phone dump shows no small-target finding for Edit note, Delete entry, Strikethrough, Highlight and Inline code, confirmed in the phone check (10.47).
